_comment: Per-provider tool-name rewrite rules + idiom translation notes applied to agent and command bodies at render time. Source bodies use Claude Code tool names (capitalized) and Claude idioms (e.g. 'Load skills/X/SKILL.md', 'spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/X.md'). The renderer uses tool_rewrites to describe the tool-name mapping, and idiom_notes to describe the brighter conventions for skill loading and subagent spawning.

claude._comment: Identity — source already uses Claude Code tool names and idioms.

opencode._comment: opencode exposes lowercase tool names; the `task` tool spawns subagents; `question` is the quiz tool. Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash stay lowercase. Skills are loaded via the `skill` tool named `SKILL.md` filename form (e.g. `skill({ name: 'reviewer-mindset' })`). Subagents are spawned via `task({ name: '<agent-name>' })` — no path arg, the name only.
idiom_notes: · **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`, invoke the opencode `skill` tool with the skill's folder name, e.g. `skill({ name: '<name>' })`. The skill body lives at `.opencode/skills/dev-team-agents/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` and opencode resolves it by name.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body says `spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/<X>.md`, treat it as `task({ name: '<X>' })` in opencode — subagents are registered as `.opencode/agents/<X>.md` and resolved by name only, no path.

· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real paths materialized at install time; access them with the `read` tool the same way Claude would.

codex._comment: Codex uses function-calling tools: apply_patch (file edits), spawn_agent (subagent), update_plan (plan/todos), Read (files), Bash (shell), Glob/Grep (search), WebSearch (web). Codex has no structured quiz tool — AskUserQuestion falls back to plain text. Skills are read as files at .dev-team-agents/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md.
idiom_notes: · **Tool names.** Claude Code tool names are used in this body. Their Codex equivalents:
· `Bash` — shell commands (replaces `Glob` and `Grep` for file search)
· Plain text — ask the user questions (replaces `AskUserQuestion`; Codex has no quiz tool)
· **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, open and read the file `.dev-team-agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with `Read`. Codex has no dedicated skill tool.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body says `spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/<X>.md`, use `spawn_agent({ agent_type: '<X>' })`. The agent definition is at `.codex/agents/<X>.toml` — resolved by name, not path.
· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/some-file.md`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real files. Read them with `Read`.
· **Plan gate.** Commands with a plan gate: use Codex's native plan mode for complex tasks. For simple tasks, execute directly. Use `update_plan` to present a plan.
· **Task arguments.** `$ARGUMENTS` in command bodies = the user's free-form input after the slash command. Use it as the task description.
